newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended Friday firmly down as hopes of an early interest rate cut faded and gold shares also ended soft, but off their day lows, as they ignored a firmer bullion price, dealers said.
Dealers said futures players were directing trade as they cut long positions, putting pressure on equities.

"The market is looking very distressed. The market firmed yesterday on expectations of an early rate cut. We now don't see it coming too soon," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.

First quarter gross domestic product growth fell 0.8 percent largely hit by the agricultural sector. Excluding agriculture, non-agricultural GDP recorded a positive growth rate of 1.4 percent in the first quarter agriculture came in atone percent.

Dealers said the GDP figure showed that manufacturing and provision of electricity was proceeding well and therefore reducing interest rates would not necessarily have the desired effect of stimulating the economy.
Instead it would feed through to money supply and inflation.
Trade was thin and volatile with only 485 million rand worth of shares trade.
Gold shares refused to ride on bullion's recovery as players were wary of the platinum-inspired rally. Dealers said the market felt the rally was not related to bullion fundamentals.
The market was seen soft next week with occasional bounces after the GDP figure.
The industrial index dropped 77.7 points, or 0.93 percent, to 8,240.2 points, the gold index shed 7.8 points to 1,173.8 points and the all-share index was down 53.0 points to 7,021.7 points.
Multisource surged to a new year high after an announcement that the company was on the verge of a restructuring. It rallied 65.71 percent, or 230 cents, to 580 cents.
Consmining was the most active share traded and lost three cents to 78 cents as players struggle to understand complex relations with JCI, Saflife, Randgold and JCI chairman Mzi Khumalo.
Iscor and Sappi saw huge volumes on bookover deals. Iscor was up two cents to 303 cents and Sappi ended down 50 cents to 41 rand.
Near-dated share futures ended weak as players cut long positions. Gold also end down as investors were sceptical of a bullion price rally.
The June all-share contract last at 6,425/40 from 6,432, industrial contract is at 8,032/37 from 8,033 and gold contracts at 830/42 from 833.
